note: Physical data for the orrery info panel. Radii in km, day/year in Earth units, temperatures in °C. Figures are standard published values (NASA planetary fact sheets).

bodies.name: Sun
bodies.blurb: A G-type main-sequence star holding 99.86% of the mass of the solar system. Fuses ~600 million tonnes of hydrogen a second.

bodies.name: Mercury
bodies.blurb: The smallest planet and the closest to the Sun. No atmosphere to speak of, so its surface swings by hundreds of degrees between day and night.

bodies.name: Venus
bodies.blurb: The hottest planet — a runaway greenhouse under a CO₂ atmosphere 92 times Earth's surface pressure. Rotates backwards.
facts: Retrograde, and slower than its own year
The brightest object in our sky after the Sun and Moon

bodies.name: Earth
bodies.blurb: The only place known to hold liquid surface water and life. Its large moon stabilises the axial tilt that gives us seasons.
facts: Deflects the solar wind; drives the aurorae

bodies.name: Mars
bodies.blurb: The most explored body beyond Earth. Thin CO₂ atmosphere, polar ice caps, and clear evidence of ancient flowing water.
facts: The tallest volcano known — 22 km high
Phobos and Deimos, probably captured asteroids

bodies.name: Jupiter
bodies.blurb: More massive than every other planet combined. A gas giant with no solid surface, and a magnetic field that dwarfs Earth's.
facts: A storm wider than Earth, running for centuries
Under 10 hours — the fastest of any planet
A subsurface ocean, a leading target in the search for life

bodies.name: Saturn
bodies.blurb: The ringed planet. Its density is lower than water's, and its rings are mostly water ice spanning 280 000 km but only tens of metres thick.
facts: Mostly water ice, from grains to house-sized chunks
Thick atmosphere and liquid methane lakes
Vents water plumes from a subsurface ocean

bodies.name: Uranus
bodies.blurb: An ice giant tipped on its side — its axis lies almost in its orbital plane, so each pole spends 42 years in sunlight and 42 in darkness.
facts: Methane absorbs red light, leaving cyan

bodies.name: Neptune
bodies.blurb: The outermost planet, and the first found by mathematics rather than observation — predicted from irregularities in Uranus's orbit.
facts: Up to 2 100 km/h — the fastest in the solar system
Predicted by Le Verrier, observed in 1846
Retrograde orbit — a captured Kuiper Belt object

bodies.name: Pluto
bodies.blurb: Reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006. Its orbit is eccentric enough to bring it inside Neptune's for 20 years of each circuit.
facts: Crosses inside Neptune's — last did so 1979–1999
So large the pair orbit a point outside Pluto
